sources.entry: arowser - Agent-programmable borderless web windows for macOS, driven by a CLI designed for coding agents. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/HankMonster/arowser) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: arowser is a macOS app and CLI that opens URLs or local HTML in small borderless windows addressed by stable ids, designed so coding agents can show things to the user.
keywords: keep page in corner of screen
summary.what_it_does: The app puts a URL or local file into a window with no title bar, which can be placed and sized from the command line with options like --w, --h, --x, --y and --center. The CLI controls each window by id (open, show, hide, close, reload, list with JSON output), and ownership checks reject id-addressed commands from a different owner unless --force is given. Cookie handling offers a shared persistent jar, a private per-window jar, or a named per-profile jar, and session cookies are mirrored to disk so logins survive restarts. A built-in localhost static server can mount directories for pages that need fetch or XHR, and arowser-watch reloads a window when a local file changes. Other features include fit-to-width scaling, a mobile user agent option, error cards for unreachable URLs, session restore, a window history picker, and global hotkeys.
use_cases: let a coding agent show a dashboard or report in a corner window
live preview of a local HTML report while editing
pin notification cards from a background agent
keep a web page visible while working in other apps
serve a local data-driven page to a browser window
open and manage several isolated browser windows from scripts
notable: Agent-first CLI: windows addressed by stable ids, with owner checks so multiple agents do not interfere
Cookie mirror keeps session-cookie logins alive across app restarts
Built-in localhost static server for directories, with no auth and a 127.0.0.1-only listener
Live-reload preview via arowser-watch with no third-party watcher dependency
Ships three agent skills in skills/ (arowser, notify-user, show-info)
caveats: Uses system WebKit rather than Chromium, so Chrome-only sites may misbehave
Requires macOS 12+; notarized releases and Homebrew packaging are listed as not yet available, so building from source is needed
Served directories and the arowser:// scheme are accessible to any local process; ownership is a mistake guard, not a security boundary
